items.title: Overview
items.text:
This NTCIP Process, Control, and Information Management document was developed using the NTCIP Online Development Process.

The NTCIP Online Development Process is defined in NTCIP 8001 and NTCIP 8008. This process provides an open standards development process that accepts issues reported by the community and resolved by peer-reviewed contributions from the community. The open source process concludes with the resultant material being approved by the defined approval process.

The NTCIP Online Development Process is a streamlined process focused on gaining consensus from the technical experts of the community (e.g., those participating in the open-source development process) rather than requiring every change to occur through a formal ballot of industry managers.

NTCIP Process, Control, and Information Management documents define the practices and policies used by the NTCIP Joint Committee and its working groups in developing and maintaining NTCIP publications.

This document has been prepared for the National Transportation Communications for ITS Protocol (NTCIP) project for use by the NTCIP Joint Committee which oversees the NTCIP project, the NTCIP standard development organizations (SDOs) which jointly approve NTCIP standards, the NTCIP Coordinator who administers the project, and all other stakeholders who participate in the development and maintenance of NTCIP standards.

items.title: User Comment Instructions
items.text:
Comments can be submitted at any time. In preparation of this NTCIP standards publication, input of users and other interested parties was sought and evaluated.

Comments on open-source projects can be submitted either on the discussions or issues tab of the project.

Discussions can be initiated at any time and anyone in the community can respond, all within a public environment. Responses to discussion comments are strictly informative and may not be accurate. Discussion comments can lead to the submittal of issues that need to be resolved to clarify the standard.

Issues can be submitted at any time. Issues are triaged by the project maintainer, who will evaluate their merit, classify them (e.g., as a bug, documentation issue, omission), and in most cases respond to the submitter. Once ready, issues will be available for contributors to volunteer to address. When a volunteer has a proposed solution, it can be submitted to the project and approved in a relatively short period (when compared to the traditional standards approval process). However, updates to the projects are still version controlled so that users can reference a specific version of the project without fear of it changing.

Comments should use the templates provided on the website; otherwise they may be ignored.

items.title: Scope
items.text: This document contains the policies, processes and procedures that provide the operational framework for the development and maintenance of NTCIP standards and supporting documents. It is not a comprehensive organizational-type document or manual. It is used to establish policies that are deemed important to maintaining the integrity of the NTCIP project’s products and to define processes and procedures that ensure repeated success. The procedures described in this document are the result of a number of years of evolution, driven both by the needs of the growing and increasingly diverse community, and by experience.

items.title: Document Overview
items.text:
This document provides the framework for the development and management of the standards and other supporting documents that make up the enterprise known as the National Transportation Communications for ITS Protocol (NTCIP) joint standardization project. It has been developed for:

  1. The standards development organizations (SDOs), American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials (AASHTO), Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE), and National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA), that have joined in a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to develop NTCIP standards;
  2. The consultants, manufacturers, and public transportation professionals who participate in the development of NTCIP standards providing domain expertise, quality assurance, assistance to deployments, and ongoing standards maintenance;
  3. The United States Department of Transportation (USDOT) Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) Joint Program Office (JPO) which has sponsored much of the work; and
  4. The transportation industry as a whole that depends upon quality standards produced from this project to create operational equipment, software and systems.

The remainder of this document is broken into the following chapters:

  • General – Contains information applicable to the entire document;
  • Policies – Contains the policies of the NTCIP project;
  • Processes – Contains the processes of the NTCIP project;
  • Procedures – Contains the procedures related to the NTCIP project; and
  • Annex A – Proposals that have not yet been incorporated.
  • Annex B - Policies, processes, and procedures that have been withdrawn or superseded.

items.title: Distinction among Policies, Processes, and Procedures
items.text:
Policies, processes and procedures serve different purposes:

  • A policy is a guideline or statement of position with respect to a given topic;
  • A process is the highest level description of a large task or series of related tasks; and
  • A procedure tells how a series of tasks are performed to achieve a specific outcome. For purposes of this document, procedures can include forms, checklists, templates, or other items used in the operation of the project.

A policy can exist without an associated process or procedure, either because they are not necessary or because a specific process or procedure has not yet been developed. A policy can be associated to multiple processes and procedures.

items.title: Word Choice
items.text: Polices, processes and procedures are written in the present tense and avoid the use of the word "shall". Instead, the document uses "must" for an obligation, "must not" for a prohibition, "may" for a discretionary action and "should" for a recommendation.

items.title: Metadata
items.text:
Each policy, process, and procedure in this document has the following static metadata and values:

  • Approved By – All policies are approved by the process defined in this document
  • Contact – The contact for each policy contained in this document is the NTCIP Coordinator
  • Applies To – The policies defined in this document apply to the NTCIP Joint Committee and its working groups.

Each policy, process, and procedure in this document has the following additional metadata:

  • Section Number and Title – As shown in the document; the title is not to be excessively long.
  • Effective Date – Date when the policy took effect.
  • Last Reviewed/Updated – Date when the policy was last reviewed or updated.
  • Details – i.e., the text of the policy, process, or procedure, which should include: a) the situation(s) when it does or does not apply, b) the major conditions or restrictions and c) any exclusions or special situations.

Each policy, process, and procedure may also be associated with the following metadata:

  • Supersedes – Title and date of any policies superseded by this policy.
  • History – History of major changes to the policy.
  • Related Items – Items that have a related concern or are causally connected.

items.title: Terms
items.text:
For the purposes of this document, the following terms and definitions apply. Terms not defined here are used in accordance with their definitions in ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765. Words not defined here or in ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765 are used in accordance with their definitions in Webster’s New Collegiate Dictionary.

Term Definition Comment A submission from an individual or company during a review period of a work item. A comment may take the form of a question, a confirmation, or suggest a change to the work item under review. Contributor An individual who contributes to the development of NTCIP standards or related documents. Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) The application of advanced information processing and communications, sensing, and control technologies to surface transportation with the objective of promoting more efficient use of the existing highway and transportation network, increasing safety and mobility, and decreasing the environmental cost of travel. Interoperability The ability of two or more systems or components to exchange information and use the information that has been exchanged.From IEEE Standards Dictionary, Glossary of Terms and Definitions. Liaison An individual representing an organization with special interest in the NTCIP project identified by the NTCIP JC Chair as a member of the NTCIP JC. Liaisons do not have voting privileges. National Transportation Communications for ITS Protocol (NTCIP) The family of protocols that provide common control and data collection services as well as accommodating various system topologies and data routing duties. NTCIP Coordinator Administrative lead for the NTCIP project. Coordinates the various NTCIP activities, directs consultants, and reports status to the USDOT. Minor corrections or additions to the policies and procedures may be approved by the NTCIP Coordinator. NTCIP Joint Committee (JC) The NTCIP JC is made up of 18 voting members with one-third (⅓) each being designated by AASHTO, ITE and NEMA. NTCIP JC oversees the activities of NTCIP Working Groups (WGs), reviews work items produced by the WGs, and determines if the work items are suitable for distribution through the memberships of the NTCIP SDOs for review, comment, and approval. NTCIP JC Chair The individual who leads the NTCIP Joint Committee. NTCIP SDO One of AASHTO, ITE and NEMA. Protocol A specific set of rules, procedures and conventions defining the format and timing of data transmissions between devices that must be accepted and used to understand each other. Proxy Vote A vote granted to someone other than the voting member or the voting member's designated alternate. Proxy votes are not allowed. SDO Staff An employee of an SDO that is a non-voting member of the NTCIP JC. Simple Majority More than half the votes cast, not counting abstentions, when a quorum is present. For example, if there are 15 voting members present at a meeting and the quorum requirement is met, then a vote of five yeas, four nays and six abstentions results in a motion passing. In the same meeting, a vote of five yeas, five nays, and five abstentions results in a motion failing because a majority was not achieved. Two-Thirds Majority More than or equal to two-thirds of the votes cast, not counting abstentions, when a quorum is present. For example, if there are 15 voting members present at a meeting and the quorum requirement is met, then a vote of eight yeas, four nays and three abstentions results in a motion passing (8/12). In the same meeting, a vote of seven yeas, four nays, and four abstentions results in a motion failing because a two-thirds majority was not achieved (7/11). Unanimity All voting members must be in favor of the motion. For example, if there are six voting members, all six must vote in favor for the motion to pass. User An individual who directly or whose organization uses, specifies or creates NTCIP devices or systems. User Comment A comment from a user, however, there is no real distinction in how comments or user comments are treated in the NTCIP project. Work Item A deliverable assigned to a Working Group by the NTCIP Joint Committee. Working Group A technical subcommittee of the NTCIP Joint Committee that is responsible for the development and maintenance of a standard or related documents. Working Group Chair The individual(s) who lead an NTCIP working group. There may be co-chairs of an NTCIP working group.

items.title: Openness
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 Supersedes: NTCIP Consensus-Based Organization

Participation in the NTCIP standards process is open to anyone materially interested in its work. There are no fees for participation nor are there any requirements for membership in any organization.

New and revamped NTCIP efforts are publicized within industry publications and discussed at industry meetings to encourage broad stakeholder input.

Membership lists for each active WG are maintained and available upon request, along with each member's affiliation.

items.title: Lack of Dominance
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 Supersedes: NTCIP Consensus-Based Organization

The NTCIP effort ensures a lack of dominance by any single interest category, individual, or organization by ensuring that all key decisions are made by consensus vote with a balanced voting membership and a defined appeals process.

items.title: Balance
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 Supersedes: NTCIP Consensus-Based Organization

The NTCIP structure attempts to respect the ANSI requirements for balance, which requires that no single interest category should constitute more than ⅓rd of the membership when dealing with safety-related standards. ANSI indicates that the following categories should be "considered":

  • producer,
  • user, and
  • general interest

Within the NTCIP JC, balance is achieved by refining these three categories as follows:

  • NEMA (generally reflecting producers),
  • AASHTO (generally reflecting users), and
  • ITE (generally reflecting general interest).

NTCIP groups under the NTCIP JC use the three ANSI interest categories directly.

For JC Discussion

Some have complained about how the current voting memberships are granted while public/private membership split does not satisfy the ANSI requirements. In addition, reaching quorum has also been a challenge at times. This text represents the current position of the WG on how to overcome these problems.

items.title: Coordination and harmonization
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

The NTCIP effort will coordinate with other SDOs, as deemed appropriate, to ensure that conflicts and overlaps among standards are avoided to the extent practical. In particular, efforts will be made to promote harmonization among the standards of the following SDOs:

  • AASHTO
  • IEEE
  • IETF
  • ISO
  • ITE
  • NEMA
  • SAE
  • W3C

items.title: Notification of Standards Development
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 Supersedes: NTCIP Consensus-Based Organization

The NTCIP effort will announce its major actions in major industry publications and websites, such as the ITE Journal and the ITE Website. Major actions include:

  • The start of a new or renewed standards effort
  • The start of a user comment draft (when using the traditional approval process)
  • The start of the industry approval process (for a full standard)

items.title: Consideration of views and objections
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 Supersedes: NTCIP Consensus-Based Organization

Written comments and objections submitted on any NTCIP document or proposed effort will be recorded by a defined process (e.g., directly by NTCIP staff, through online management through GitHub Issues), which will identify a target time (e.g., one week) for the comment to be triaged and an acknowledgement sent. The acknowledgement may include a response (i.e., in the case of a simple issue) but will more often need to describe the process that will be used to address the comment (e.g., identify the WG that will be notified, whether that WG has a planned meeting, etc.). Once the review process is complete, the commenter will be notified of the resolution.

Unresolved objections, along with the proposed response, will be reported to the parent approval body and members will be allowed to change their vote.

items.title: Evidence of Consensus
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 Supersedes: NTCIP Consensus-Based Organization

Consensus is demonstrated for NTCIP documents based on the type of vote, as defined in the procedures.

The NTCIP effort will maintain records of votes, comments, and objections for a minimum of seven years.

items.title: Appeals
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

Entities that are directly and materially interested in and who have been or will be adversely affected by any procedural action or inaction by the NTCIP effort can submit a written appeal to the NTCIP coordinator, any of the three SDOs, or to the chair of the JC. The appeals process will consider the perspectives of all involved in the process.

Procedural appeals relate to whether the policies, processes, and procedures defined by this document were adequately followed or if documented failures were significant enough to call the result into question. A documented fixed fee may be associated with filing an appeal.

items.title: Patent Policy
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026
  • Participants in the development of Standards, as well as the users of Standards, may have an interest in knowing whether there are provisions in a Standard incorporating someone’s intellectual property, which may require permission to use someone’s proprietary technology and possibly pay compensation for that privilege. The policies of NEMA and ANSI, as well as international Standards organizations, recognize that it is permissible to draft a Standard that includes the use of someone’s patent claims if technical reasons justify it, but Standards developing committees may prefer to avoid incorporating proprietary technology once they know of it.
  • The primary concern of these policies is the identification of essential patent claims. NEMA has defined an essential patent as a claim contained in a patent or published patent application, the use of which is necessary to create a compliant implementation of a mandatory provision in the normative clauses of a NEMA Standard or proposed NEMA Standard when there is no commercially and technically feasible non-infringing alternative. Participants in this standards developing process are obligated to disclose essential patent claims of which they have knowledge. A participant may self-disclose any essential patent claims they or their employer own or control, or a participant may ask NTCIP representatives to query whether another participant or third-party owns or controls any essential patent claims. The obligation to disclose is a continuing one, both before and after a Standard is published.
  • Disclosure must identify the patent or patent application, the part of the standard incorporating an essential patent claim, and an assurance that a license to use the essential patent claims will be made available either on reasonable terms and conditions that are demonstrably free of any unfair discrimination or without compensation but with other reasonable terms and conditions that are demonstrably free of unfair discrimination.

items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

NTCIP documents will not include terms or conditions that are primarily contractual or commercial in nature as opposed to technical, engineering, or scientific in nature. For example, NTCIP documents will not include requirements related to specific products or services, warranties, prices, conformity assessment firms, etc.

items.title: Antitrust Policy
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

The NTCIP effort is committed to compliance with antitrust laws and all meetings will be conducted in strict compliance with these antitrust guidelines. Further if an item comes up for which a participant has a conflict of interest, that member should declare the conflict of interest on the matter and recuse themselves from action on that item.

The following discussions and/or exchanges of information by or among competitors concerning are prohibited:

  • Prices, price changes, price quotations, pricing policies, discounts, payment terms, credit, allowances or terms or conditions of sale;
  • Profits, profit margins or cost data;
  • Market shares, sales territories or markets;
  • The allocation of customer territories;
  • Selection, rejection or termination of customers or suppliers;
  • Restricting the territory or markets in which a company may sell services or products;
  • Restricting the customers to whom a company may sell;
  • Unreasonable restrictions on the development or use of technologies; or
  • Any matter which is inconsistent with the proposition that each company must exercise its independent business judgement in pricing its service or products, dealing with its customers and suppliers and choosing the markets in which it will compete.

items.title: Types of Documents
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2017 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

For JC Review

The WG recommends eliminating Amendments and Errata and to replace them with previously approved semantic version numbers. In other words, rather than issuing a partial document as an amendment, the document should be revised and the semantic version number updated as appropriate based on the extent of changes. The new edition can then be approved using the IFR or traditional process. IFR documents can still be Word/PDF documents.

The NTCIP Effort recognizes the following types of documents:

  • Technical specifications: Documents that contain requirements (i.e., "shall" statements) that relate to products within the ITS industry.
  • Process, control, and management documents: Documents that define rules for the NTCIP effort, such as this document. Other such documents include documents that define details about the formats of NTCIP documents, rules for NTCIP MIBs, rules for using GitHub, etc. (i.e., 8000 series)
  • Informational Reports: Documents that provide useful information for the industry but do not provide any requirements (i.e, 9000 series)
  • Registries: Documents or websites that require frequent updates to reflect requests (e.g., the registry of manufacturer IDs).

Note

The NTCIP effort historically supported amendment documents. These were used to correct technical errors, ambiguities, and/or editorial mistakes contained in published documents in a timely fashion. Early versions of these documents were published as short stand-alone paper documents. As the world migrated to electronic formats, the amendments were published as new minor editions of the major version of the standard. The migration to semantic version numbers rather than the prior versioning scheme negates the need to maintain the concept of an amendment. Instead, if a correction is needed to any document, the necessary edits should be made to the original document (i.e., either the Word document or website) along with an appropriately updated semantic version number and an explanation of the change (within the Annexes). The new version can be quickly approved using the IFR approval process, and if desired, the IFR approval can be followed by traditional standards approval process to demonstrate greater acceptance.

items.title: Standardization Levels
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2017 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 History: Added IFR in 2026

The NTCIP effort recognizes three levels of standardization for its documents (other than registries), as discussed below. Not all documents are expected to become standards.

  • (Full) Standard: A document that has been balloted and approved by all three SDOs through the traditional industry-wide balloting process. Standards are intended to show broad industry support for documents that 1) are considered very stable and will not need a major update for several years and/or 2) represent a significant body of work that should be recognized as a solid baseline while work continues in the development of new features.
  • Recommended Standard: A document that has received the support of the Joint Committee on the NTCIP to be sent to industry ballot. Recommended Standards are primarily intended for 1) an interim stage on the way to full standardization, and 2) the final stage for process, control, and management documents as these are intended to be documents for internal NTCIP management and generally do not benefit from broader industry ballots because all of the stakeholders are internal to the NTCIP.
  • Interim Document for Field Release (IFR): A document that represents current thinking of the NTCIP organization and met the defined criteria for being ready for implementation and field use. The Interim Document for Field Release stage exists to provide a streamlined standardization process. While it reflects a lower level of consensus, it allows for faster adoption of a document. When combined with the online development process (as defined in NTCIP 8008), it can create a much more agile development approach for standardization that promotes fast incremental development. Faster development results in increased risks due to shorter review cycles, but in an environment with rapidly changing technology, a faster process may be deemed appropriate for some efforts.

items.title: Designators for Documents
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2017 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 History: Changed to semantic versioning in 2026

All NTCIP documents will follow a common formulaic naming convention that will

  • Indicate that it is a part of the NTCIP family of standards
  • Provide a unique number that can be used to refer to the document content (regardless of approval stage or version number)
  • Provide a version number that indicates the semantic versioning of the document
  • Indicate the approval stage of the document, if not a full standard
  • Provide a title that describes the document content

items.title: Code of Ethics and Conduct
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

The NTCIP community tries to maintain a positive and collaborative atmosphere for the development of standards. Participants should:

  • Disclose any personal, financial, or professional conflicts promptly and recuse yourself if necessary.
  • Prohibit bribery, gifts, or favors that could influence outcomes.
  • Respect copyrights, patents, and contributions; ensure proper attribution.
  • Adhere to all applicable laws, regulations, and SDO policies.
  • Engage in constructive dialogue, avoiding harassment, discrimination, or disruptive behavior.
  • Encourage others to voice their opinions and consider the opinions voiced.

items.title: Procedures of the NTCIP JC
items.text: This section contains the procedures that primarily address activities of the NTCIP JC.

items.title: Meeting procedures of the NTCIP JC
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2017 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

Much of the work of the NTCIP JC occurs in meetings. Meetings may take place in a face-to-face setting, through web conferencing or through a teleconference. The practices for conducting meetings of the NTCIP JC are described below.

items.title: Announcement of meetings
items.text:
The NTCIP Coordinator must announce every meeting of the NTCIP JC in coordination with the NTCIP JC chair. The announcement must include the date, time, location, and agenda.

Question

For review

Virtual meetings are to be announced at least two weeks in advance of the meeting. In-person meetings are to be announced at least six weeks in advance of the meeting.

Announcements must be made using the designated communication channels established for the NTCIP JC.

items.title: Parliamentary authority
items.text:
The parliamentary authority of the NTCIP JC follows Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised (RONR). RONR governs in all cases to which they are applicable and in which they are not inconsistent with this policies, processes and procedures document.

Question

Do we want to soften this language? Robert's rules are rather strict and constraining, and in practice are not being followed that way in hardly any of the SDOs. Perhaps something like NTCIP groups are generally governed by consensus processes and rely on Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised (RONR) when resolving conflicts and taking votes.

items.title: General
items.text:
Votes on matters before the JC may be taken either within a meeting or through an electronic ballot. Votes must not be mixed between the two methods.

For votes conducted within a committee meeting, members who are unable to attend may submit their vote by correspondence in advance of the meeting. Such correspondence votes must be received by the NTCIP JC chair or the NTCIP Coordinator (or designated recipient) prior to the start of the meeting and will be counted as if the member were present.

For votes conducted within a committee meeting, a ballot cast may be from the voting member or the voting member's designated alternate, if the voting member is not present. Proxy votes are not allowed.

For votes conducted electronically, the number of responses received must represent a quorum.

Unless otherwise specified, votes must be taken by simple majority.

Note

The following actions vary from a simple majority.

  • Approval of a Recommended Standard (RS)
  • Approval of an Interim Document for Field Release (IFR)
  • Creation of a new NTCIP group
  • Removal of a NTCIP group chair or NTCIP group vice-chair

Question

Are there any cases where we want to specify other measures, such as:

  • absolute majority: i.e., >50% of the voting membership (we would need to clarify what happens with an empty seat)
  • majority of those present: i.e., >50% of the voting members present at the meeting (which should probably be = to absolute majority with the exception of empty seats in the case of electronic ballots)

Question

Review the following three ways to initiate a vote. Are they all valid?

items.title: JC Chair initiated votes
items.text:
The chair of the NTCIP JC may initiate a vote on an issue according to the following procedure:

  1. The chair must identify the question to be asked and the ballot method to use (e.g., electronic or in-person). The information must be sent to the NTCIP Coordinator.
  2. The question will be announced to the voting membership either:
    • as an agenda item for the next meeting and followed by a period of discussion and voting at the meeting
    • via electronic means and followed by a minimum period of 30 days of discussion and two-weeks of voting

items.title: Group initiated votes
items.text:
A group may initiate a vote within the NTCIP JC as a part of a task to which it has been assigned according to the following procedure:

  1. A motion must be made by a voting member of the group to advance a report or document to its next stage through a vote by the NTCIP JC.
  2. The motion must be seconded.
  3. The motion must pass within the group by the required majority.
  4. The request for a vote within the NTCIP JC must be recorded and communicated to the NTCIP JC chair and NTCIP Coordinator.
  5. The NTCIP JC chair must identify the ballot method to use (e.g., electronic or in-meeting). The information must be sent to the NTCIP Coordinator.
  6. The question will be announced to the NTCIP JC voting membership either:
    • as an agenda item for the next meeting at least two weeks in advance of the meeting and followed by a period of discussion and voting at the meeting
    • via electronic means and followed by a minimum period of 30 days of discussion and two-weeks of voting

items.title: Member requested votes
items.text:
A voting member of the NTCIP JC may request to initiate a vote on any issue according to the following procedure:

  1. A motion must be made by a voting member of the NTCIP JC that states the question to be asked and the ballot method to use (e.g., electronic or in-person). The motion may be made at a meeting or via electronic means.
  2. The motion must be seconded.
  3. The motion must pass by simple majority.
  4. The question will be announced to the voting membership either:
    • at a meeting and followed by a period of discussion and voting at the meeting
    • as an agenda item for the next meeting and followed by a period of discussion and voting at the meeting
    • via electronic means and followed by a minimum period of two-weeks of voting

Note

This process allows issues that arise at a meeting to be voted on immediately; however, it is greatly preferred to identify issues to be voted on in advance of a meeting and to announce them as an agenda item.

items.title: Specific actions of the NTCIP JC
Creating an NTCIP group
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2017 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

There may be times when a work item to be undertaken by the NTCIP JC is not suitable for an existing NTCIP WG or that another NTCIP group is warranted. In this case, the NTCIP JC may create a new group by agreeing to and recording the following terms:

  1. The need and scope for the new group
  2. The work items to be assigned to the group
  3. The NTCIP JC voting member that will act as the group's sponsor and support its activities
  4. The number of members of each interest category to be assigned to the group

The decision to establish a new group requires at least a two-thirds (⅔s) majority.

Once established, the NTCIP JC chair assigns a chair and vice-chair of the group with input from the NTCIP JC, the SDO representatives and the NTCIP Coordinator. The NTCIP JC chair will then work with the group's chair and vice-chair to establish the group's initial voting membership.

items.title: JC assigns a work item to a WG
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2017 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

All documents developed under the oversight of the NTCIP JC begin with a proposal. Typically, a proposal comes from an existing NTCIP group but it may come from other sources such as a member of the NTCIP JC, an SDO, or the USDOT.

When a proposal is submitted to the Joint Committee, it must include the following details regarding the effort:

  1. the sponsor of the proposal;
  2. the working group, or other team, responsible for assisting the sponsor;
  3. The type of document to be produced;
  4. the scope of the proposed document;
  5. an explanation of why the document is needed;
  6. any related documents;
  7. any related working groups;
  8. the expected completion date; and
  9. an estimate of any required financial assistance.

A proposal may also contain sample text for the document. The sample text can be anything from a few words to an entire draft.

Proposals are submitted to the NTCIP Joint Committee for approval; however, most proposals should be submitted through an appropriate working group in order to show a level of consensus for the proposal.

The decision to establish a new work item requires at least a simple majority.

If the JC chooses to go forward with the proposal, the project is assigned to an appropriate WG. If no appropriate WG exists, a new working group may be formed. Once the work item is assigned to a WG and any preconditions for the proposal are met, then the proposal is approved and work may begin.

items.title: JC reviews document
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

When a document requires JC review, it is distributed to the NTCIP JC membership for review for a minimum of 30 days. Members should formulate comments and questions prior to the subsequent NTCIP JC meeting.

When the document is distributed for review, it must identify its associated approved work item and the group that prepared the document.

items.title: JC approves document for next stage
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

A meeting, web conference or teleconference is held where the WG Chair (and possibly a technical lead in the project) presents the document to the members of the NTCIP JC. The NTCIP JC asks the presentation team questions and makes comments based on their review. Any issue may be discussed regarding the document. The NTCIP JC may take a vote to advance the document to its next stage (e.g., UCD, RS, IFR). The question that is voted on may include direction to correct issues within the document prior to proceeding to the next stage. The amount of support required to pass a vote varies depending on the next stage of the work item, as follows:

  • User Comment Draft (UCD): simple majority
  • Recommended Standard (RS): two-thirds (⅔s) majority
  • Interim Document for Field Release (IFR): two-thirds (⅔s) majority

If the vote fails, the NTCIP JC will provide direction on how to proceed. This direction will typically indicate what revisions are required to make document acceptable to the NTCIP JC. The revisions may be to simply correct editorial items in the standard prior to a re-vote or there may be some more significant development to be done.

items.title: NTCIP JC Vacancies
items.text:
Question

I am not sure where this text came from. Do we want to keep?

Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2017 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026 History This procedure on NTCIP JC Vacancies was established to provide the NTCIP JC the means to fill its own vacancies on the NTCIP JC if the SDOs are unable to do so.

The procedures for membership and leadership and of the NTCIP JC are established in the MOU Section 1.0 Establishment of a Joint Committee. The MOU states that there are “18 voting members with ⅓rd each being designated by AASHTO, ITE, and NEMA.” While this is the intent, it is often the case that that an SDO is not able to immediately fill a vacancy when one occurs. In order for the NTCIP JC to be effective, its voting membership must be maintained. The steps below help ensure the NTCIP JC membership.

  1. A vacancy on the NTCIP JC may be identified by an SDO or the NTCIP Chair when they are informed by a voting member that they will no longer be participating in that capacity. A potential vacancy may also be identified by the NTCIP Chair when a voting member has not participated in three consecutive NTCIP JC meetings.
  2. The SDO that has the vacancy on the NTCIP JC is allowed up to one year to fill a vacancy.
  3. If the SDO does not fill the vacancy in one year, the NTCIP JC Chair may nominate a representative pro tem to fill the vacancy. The representative pro tem must be a member (or representative of a member organization) of the SDO that has the vacancy on the NTCIP JC. The NTCIP JC must confirm the nomination by simple majority.

items.text:
The NTCIP Coordinator must announce every meeting of each NTCIP group in coordination with the respective chair. The announcement must include the date, time, location, and agenda.

items.title: Parliamentary authority
items.text:
The parliamentary authority of an NTCIP group follows Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised (RONR). RONR governs in all cases to which they are applicable and in which they are not inconsistent with the policies, processes, and procedures defined in this document.

Question

Do we want to soften this language? Robert's rules are rather strict and constraining, and in practice are not being followed that way in hardly any of the SDOs. Perhaps something like NTCIP groups are generally governed by consensus processes and rely on Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised (RONR) when resolving conflicts and taking votes.

Acceptance Actions Between Meetings of the NTCIP WG: Acceptance actions by the NTCIP WG are those when a vote is taken to accept a WGD as a pUCD, pRS or pRE. Typically, acceptance actions are completed as part of an NTCIP WG meeting. There are circumstances, however, when the NTCIP WG may determine that it is prudent to complete an acceptance action outside of a meeting. This may be done because the NTCIP WG members need more time to review a proposed document before voting, there are not enough voting members at the meeting to perform the vote, or some other reason. In such cases, an electronic ballot may be used outside of the NTCIP WG meeting as follows:

  1. A motion must be made that an electronic ballot be taken to accept the pUCD, pRS or pRE. The motion must be recorded at the meeting and include the details of when and how the ballot will be performed. Electronic balloting may include email, a polling website, or some other method.
  2. The motion must be seconded.
  3. The motion must pass by simple majority.
  4. No split vote between a meeting and electronic voting is allowed. All voting must take place during a meeting NTCIP WG or electronically outside of the meeting but not both.

items.title: Group drafts/revises document
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

After a work item proposal has been approved, the designated group begins the task of creating the draft document and building consensus based on the input from the group members. Often, a paid consultant serves as the editor; although, the work may also be done on a volunteer basis by group members.

Early drafts can be incomplete, address certain features or areas of the work item, or be in a non-compliant format. The editor is responsible for ensuring that the document evolves into the correct format, as defined by NTCIP 8002, and that all necessary sections are drafted.

The work to develop this draft can either follow the traditional process (e.g., using Word documents) or follow the online process described in NTCIP 8008. The editor is responsible for ensuring that the group's input is incorporated into the document and that the document is developed in a timely manner while maintaining a high quality.

items.title: Group collects and resolves comments
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

In addition to internal group discussions, the group is responsible for collecting and resolving written comments from the larger industry community. These comments frequently include comments from group members performing detailed reviews of the document at key points during the development cycle. The group can collect these comments in one of two ways:

  • In the traditional standards development process, the NTCIP JC approves a UCD, which represents a substantially complete draft, with a defined commenting period. All written comments received during this period are carefully managed and formal responses are prepared. Comments may be sent directly to the group or forwarded through SDO Staff to the group. The group is responsible for adjudicating the comments and preparing formal responses, which are recorded by the editor and managed by the NTCIP Coordinator.
  • In the online standards development process, the document is always available online and its associated GitHub environment allows for the submission of comments (a.k.a., issues) at any time. These comments and responses are managed by the GitHub environment automatically. Prior to approval, the document is released as a "-ucd" pre-release version for a minimum of 30 days.

Question

I added a "-ucd" pre-release to be used as a warning of a pending approval period and asking for final comments with a minimum 30-day window. Is this appropriate?

The group collects, organizes, and adjudicates all comments received during the commenting period. The comments may be editorial, technical, simple or substantial in nature. A comment may be “rejected” based on the consensus of the group. Some of the reasons that a comment may be rejected are that the group may disagree technically with the proposed change, the group may decide that the proposed change is out of scope for the work item being developed, or the comment may not be suitable because of other corrective actions taken by the group. A comment is “accepted” when it is the consensus of the group that the suggested change or issue is appropriate. Often, comments submitted include suggested changes to the text of the standard. Such changes are taken as recommendations but the group may accept the comment but modify the corrective measures suggested (i.e., "accepted as modified"). The adjudications of the comments must be posted on the GitHub repository, provided directly to the commenter(s), recorded otherwise within the NTCIP records, or some combination thereof.

items.title: Group approves document for next stage
items.text:
Parameter Value Effective Date: September 30, 2026 Last Reviewed/Updated: September 30, 2026

Once a group has consensus on the document and the document conforms to NTCIP 8002, it takes a vote to advance the document to its next stage. The amount of support required to pass a vote varies depending on the next stage of the work item, as follows:

  • Pre-User Comment Draft (pUCD): simple majority
  • Pre-Recommended Standard (pRS): two-thirds (⅔s) majority
  • Pre-Interim Document for Field Release (pIFR): two-thirds (⅔s) majority
  • Interim Document for Field Release (IFR) by a working group: two-thirds (⅔s) majority
  • Interim Document for Field Release (IFR) by a maintenance group : unanimity

Question

Are we good with unanimity for the IFR by a maintenance group?

If the vote passes, the document is advanced to the next stage. If the vote fails, the group will need to continue working on the document until consensus is achieved.

items.title: Procedures of the SDOs
items.text: This section contains the procedures of the SDOs.

items.title: SDOs distribute document
items.text: At defined stages, the NTCIP SDOs distribute the document to the members of their organizations for industry review. The exact procedures are defined by the SDOs themselves.

items.title: Industry approves document as full standard
items.text: The SDOs manage the approval from industry according to their own approval (or ballot) process.

items.title: SDOs publish document
items.text: Once a document has been approved for final release, the NTCIP SDOs must update the document (i.e., showing its new status and any other final editorial changes) and make the document publicly available (e.g., through a designated website).

items.title: Procedure for approving an NTCIP standard
items.text:
The procedure for approving an NTCIP standard is followed to produce a full standard with a Recommended Standard (RS) produced as an interim step. The procedure is as follows:

Question

Replace the following with a GraphViz figure

Figure 3: Standards development process
  1. The NTCIP JC assigns a work item to a WG
  2. WG drafts/revises document
  3. SDOs distribute document
  4. WG collects and resolves comments (resolution can include deferring issues to a future version)
  5. WG approves document as pre-Recommended Standard (pre-RS)
  6. JC reviews pre-RS document
  7. JC approves document as a Recommended Standard (RS)
  8. SDO publishes as an RS
  9. SDO distributes RS for industry review
  10. Industry approves document as full standard
  11. SDO publishes full standard

items.title: Procedure for approving an NTCIP Interim Document for Field Release (IFR)
items.text:
The IFR approval process is designed for quick approval and release and avoids delays due to lengthy ballot periods and editorial review. The IFR process can be particularly responsive to user needs when combined with the online development process, which allows the administrative aspects of the user comment period to be condensed using online tools rather than relying on more traditional processes. However, the IFR process can also be applied to processes using traditional MS Word documents.

The basic IFR approval procedure is as follows:

  1. The NTCIP JC assigns a work item to a WG with permission to use the IFR process
  2. If new major version (i.e., new document or not backwards compatible)
    1. WG drafts/revises document
    2. SDOs distributes UCD document
    3. WG collects and resolves UCD comments (resolution can include deferring issues to a future version)
    4. WG approves document as pre-IFR
    5. JC reviews pre-IFR document
    6. JC approves document as IFR (major version)
  3. If minor version (i.e., backwards compatible with one or more additional features or corrections)
    1. WG revises document
    2. SDOs distributes UCD document
    3. WG collects and resolves comments (resolution can include deferring issues to a future version)
    4. WG approves document as IFR (minor version)
  4. If patch version (i.e., backwards compatible with one or more corrections)
    1. Maintenance Group (MG) revises document
    2. SDOs distributes UCD document
    3. MG collects and resolves comments (resolution can include deferring issues to a future version)
    4. MG approves document as IFR (patch version)
  5. SDO publishes IFR
  6. A group or any of its parents may rescind one of its approved IFRs at any time (the version is retained in history but is marked as rescinded).
